# `overflow-before-clamp`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: correctness · Profile: none · Default: warning · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports direct checked integer addition inside `@min`, or subtraction inside
`@max`, when the arithmetic can overflow or underflow before the clamp is
evaluated.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Zig evaluates the arithmetic argument before calling the clamp builtin. A bound
such as `@min(limit, offset + amount)` therefore does not prevent `offset +
amount` from trapping.

## When it fires

The rule requires two runtime-derived operands with locally visible integer
types. This excludes small literal lookaheads into already materialized
collections and constants known at compile time. Sums that cannot wrap are
skipped: lengths of objects in memory plus literals (`a.len + b.len`), and a
cursor bounded by a length in the enclosing `while` condition plus a length or
literal (`while (i < data.len)` around `@min(data.len, i + buf.len)`).
Arithmetic in signed types of 64 or more bits is not reported: coordinates and
deltas widened to `i64` stay far from its range, and `@max(0, a - b)` is the
right clamp for signed values. Saturating or wrapping operators, checked
arithmetic APIs, a visible early-exit guard, and an earlier `assert` that
evaluates the same sum keep the expression clean.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn clampedEnd(start: u32, len: u32, max: u32) u32 {
    return @min(start + len, max);
}
```
